notes: The recordstore check RUNS the agent's lib/store.js and tools/cli.js, so it runs them only in child processes of a private temp sandbox (direct child of the OS temp dir) with a scrubbed environment (PATH, HOME inside the sandbox, TMPDIR, LANG), a timeout per call and, on Linux, bubblewrap (read-only host file system, no network) or `unshare --net`; a Node child also gets Node's permission model confined to the sandbox. The verdict is the file-system state the check reads itself plus a per-call marker, so an early exit(0), a swallowed throw or a no-op cannot pass.

The clientkit check (eval 2) uses the same confinement as the recordstore check: it RUNS the agent's lib/*.js only in sandboxed child processes (one per scenario; scrubbed environment, timeout, bubblewrap or `unshare --net` where available, Node's permission model for the Node child). Each child prints the values it observed after a per-call marker and the parent compares them with the expected values, so an early exit(0), a swallowed throw or a no-op cannot pass.

Remaining gap: on a platform with neither bubblewrap nor unshare (macOS, Windows) the file system and the network are not enforced for the child; only the scrubbed environment, the timeout, the sandbox working directory and (Node 24 and later) the permission model apply. SKILL_CHECK_CONFINEMENT=none|unshare|bwrap forces a tier.
